subsystems.name: Mid-infrared observatory
subsystems.role: collects thermal emission from a target while avoiding Earth's own infrared glow.

subsystems.name: Target catalogue and observing plan
subsystems.role: selects stars, exoplanets or galaxies where a large energy economy might be detectable.

subsystems.name: Data reduction pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw detector counts into calibrated flux measurements.

subsystems.name: Natural-source models
subsystems.role: predict what the target would look like without any engineering.
parts: debris disk and dust emission models

subsystems.name: Signal discrimination
subsystems.role: decides whether any excess is real, significant and not natural.

subsystems.name: Follow-up spectroscopy

buildSteps.title: Select targets
buildSteps.detail: Compile a list of nearby stars, transiting exoplanets or galaxies that could host a large-scale energy economy. Prioritise those with known planets in the habitable zone or unusual infrared colours.

buildSteps.title: Observe in the mid-infrared
buildSteps.detail: Use a space telescope with cryogenic optics to measure the target's flux at several wavelengths, ideally across its orbital phase.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and subtract backgrounds
buildSteps.detail: Remove zodiacal light, telescope emission and other instrumental backgrounds using reference observations and standard stars.

buildSteps.title: Search for excess
buildSteps.detail: Compare the measured flux to the expected emission from the star alone. An excess above the stellar photosphere is the candidate signal.

buildSteps.title: Model natural explanations
buildSteps.detail: Run radiative-transfer models of dust, debris disks, atmospheres and background galaxies to see if they can reproduce the excess.

buildSteps.title: Test significance
buildSteps.detail: Use statistical methods to quantify how unlikely the excess is under natural models, and check for instrumental artifacts or background sources.

buildSteps.title: Follow up with spectroscopy
buildSteps.detail: If a candidate survives, obtain a mid-infrared spectrum. A smooth, featureless excess near the equilibrium temperature of a large energy economy would strengthen the technosignature case.

buildSteps.title: Publish and replicate
buildSteps.detail: Release the data and analysis so other teams can verify the result with independent observations.

prerequisites.tech: Mid-infrared space telescopes with cryogenic detectors
prerequisites.why: Earth's atmosphere blocks much of the mid-infrared, so the search needs cold space-based observatories such as Spitzer and JWST.

prerequisites.tech: Radiative-transfer models of dust and atmospheres
prerequisites.why: without them, any infrared excess could not be tested against natural explanations.
to separate a planet's waste heat from its star's light, especially for habitable-zone planets.

prerequisites.tech: Large-scale data archives and analysis tools
prerequisites.why: searches rely on re-analysing archival survey data from missions like WISE and Spitzer.

prerequisites.tech: A confirmed detection of any technosignature
prerequisites.why: no waste-heat technosignature has yet been confirmed, so the search remains exploratory.

pathway.milestone: archival searches of Spitzer, WISE and JWST data for anomalous mid-infrared excess
pathway.unlocks: statistical limits on how common large-scale waste heat is.

pathway.milestone: dedicated mid-infrared surveys of nearby stars and galaxies with improved sensitivity
pathway.unlocks: a systematic census of potential technosignatures.

pathway.milestone: next-generation space telescopes with larger apertures and better coronagraphy
pathway.unlocks: ability to detect faint waste heat from individual exoplanets.

pathway.milestone: follow-up spectroscopy of a candidate excess
pathway.unlocks: confirmation or rejection of an artificial origin, and the first direct evidence of an advanced civilisation.
